did: Ordered Ney to attack Mack (Swabia, then Munich); the whole army marched to the guns onto Bavarian soil. Then opened the Ledger economy book.
expected: The order preview (MUSTER) to warn me that corps standing on allied Bavarian soil are paid 'by contract' at a cost; the treasury readout stayed sane.
saw: The turn-1 dispatch said +828 next turn; after two battles the top line reads 492 gold (-480 next turn). Only the Ledger Economy book explains it: Campaign pay -1776g for seven corps on allied soil, plus Grande Armee surcharge -738g and over-limit surcharge -204g (181,967 men vs a 130,000 limit). The muster preview warned about materiel losses but never about campaign pay, so I committed 7 corps to Bavaria without knowing it would bankrupt me in one turn.

action_text: type how do I get to Vienna
did: Typed 'how do I get to Vienna' hoping for a route.
expected: A route, or the next province on the road to Vienna.
saw: The whole ~11,000-px command reference dumped into the command window (a different answer than the one-line replies other questions get); nothing about Vienna or the road to it.

action_text: type what if Massena attacks Archduke John
did: After scouting Tyrol (Archduke John ~20,000, Mack ~837), asked 'what if Massena attacks Archduke John'.
expected: A verdict that matches the numbers: my 41,566 (up to 58,452) against his 20,000.
saw: 'the balance of force looks unfavorable' beside Massena 41,566 / expect 49,512 vs 20,000 men. The standing modifiers (+25% mountains, +10% his stance) do not obviously turn 2.5:1 into unfavorable, and no number says by how much; I could not tell whether to trust the word or the figures.

did: Earlier chose 'Not Now' on Prussia's Open Borders proposal (after a 'Let Talleyrand haggle (1 DP)' that answered 'no counter Prussia could take — the offer stands' and left the popup open). Later clicked The Cabinet to look for the Laws.
expected: 'Not Now' to mean set it aside; the Cabinet to open.
saw: The Cabinet refuses to open: 'An unanswered envoy awaits your reply. Reopen Envoys before starting a new diplomatic action.' So 'Not Now' is not really postponing - it blocks all diplomacy until I answer. Also the haggle button gave no visible result beyond that one line, and I cannot tell if it cost the DP.

did: In the peace preview for Austria (generous suggested terms), clicked 'Adjust terms' hoping to edit the terms (e.g. drop the release of Archduke Charles, add a province demand).
expected: An editor over the peace terms shown.
saw: A different wizard: 'Shall we discuss concessions, Sire?' with 'Let me suggest regions to offer' / 'offer gold' / 'Offer Action Points' - it reads as if I would be GIVING territory to Austria, not demanding it. There was no Back button; I escaped out. 'Harsher terms' only added 300 gold/turn and the acceptance fell to 3 REJECT (war age penalty), with no way to see why or to ask for a province.

did: Peace preview for Austria: clicked 'Adjust terms', got the 'DIPLOMATIC PROPOSAL - Austria: Shall we discuss concessions, Sire?' dialog. Pressed Escape twice.
expected: Escape (or a Back/Close control) to leave a dialog I did not want.
saw: Escape does nothing; the dialog has only three buttons (discuss territory / offer gold / Offer Action Points) and no Back, Close or Cancel. I cannot leave without picking an answer that sounds like paying Austria.

did: Clicked 'Let Talleyrand haggle (1 DP)' on Austria's peace offer (and earlier on Prussia's open borders and Austria's armistice).
expected: Some counter-offer, or at least a reason it is offered at all.
saw: All three times: 'Talleyrand finds no counter Austria could take - the offer stands.' The button promises a counter and has never produced one; I stopped trusting it. It would help if it were greyed out with the reason when it cannot yield anything.

action_text: type what if Massena attacks Kutuzov
did: On turn 5 accepted Austria's 'Peace Treaty on the held line' (keeping Vienna, Bohemia, Carniola, Hungary). On turn 6 tried to attack Kutuzov, who stands at Moravia.
expected: To be able to attack the Russians I am still at war with, or to have been told at the peace table that I could not.
saw: 'Ney/Davout/Lannes/Murat/Napoleon: cannot march - the field is on soil we are not at war with.' Moravia is Austrian soil and I just made peace with Austria, so the Russian armies (Kutuzov 34k, Buxhowden 22k) sit safe there next to Vienna and Hungary. The peace proposal's 'Political Consequences' never mentioned that signing would shelter my enemies; only discovered a turn later. Also the Russians attacked Murat in Hungary from there and my whole army was dragged to Hungary automatically.

did: After an enemy-phase report I pressed 'Continue', then Escape to dismiss the battle replay, then Escape again to be sure.
expected: Escape to close the replay, and a second Escape to do nothing harmful.
saw: The replay sometimes needs one Escape (skip animation) and a second to close, sometimes just one; a further Escape then opens the Pause menu (Save/Load/Quit to Desktop). I opened the pause menu by accident three times (again at #263). No indicator tells me how many dismissals are pending; the queued replays from two enemy-phase battles stack behind each other too.

action_text: type what if Murat attacks Hanover
did: Declared war on Hanover (Talleyrand's objection said alarm 45 -> 73 and a league would gather; I proceeded). Took Osnabruck with Murat, then ordered the army to march on Hanover.
expected: A war with Hanover on the war panel, a known number of provinces to take, and the alarm bought something for the price of 28 points.
saw: Hanover's other provinces were already Prussian (it had made peace with Prussia the turn before, ceding the capital); my one capture of Osnabruck seems to have ended the nation, the war panel only lists 'War with Britain', the order 'march to Hanover' now said 'France is at peace with Prussia, the order would first put a declaration of war to you', and Holland asked for Osnabruck at once. The Cabinet and the Intelligence book still showed Hanover as a 6-region nation on the turn I declared. Result: +28 alarm and a brewing nine-court league for one province; nothing on the declaration screens told me Prussia had already carved it up.

did: With my army shattered by Bagration and the league formed, opened the whole-table settlement with the Fourth Coalition (8 courts) and pressed 'More generous' once to bring Austria and Russia to the table.
expected: Gold or concessions to move the two holdouts up toward 50, or a plain statement of what they want.
saw: Every court was handed 100 gold and the table said 'The accord can bear no further terms, Sire' (eight clauses full), while Austria (-4/50) and Russia (22/50) still read 'Blocker: Settlement legitimacy - the terms claim a victory the field has not delivered'. A white peace was a 'victory not delivered', and no screen says what would fix it (more generous cannot, adding demands is locked). I could not tell whether to keep paying, drop Austria and Russia, or give up; I backed out with a draft that paid every enemy court and bought nothing.

did: Ordered Soult (at Franconia, with Bohemia occupied by Mack) 'march to Vienna' to reinforce a beaten army.
expected: A short march along my own road, or a warning before it commits that the road is cut.
saw: The order committed at once with the route printed only afterwards: 'Berlin -> Brandenburg -> Posen -> Silesia -> Podolia -> Moravia -> Vienna' - a six-province loop through Prussia and Poland and past the Russian army, because Bohemia was held by the enemy. I had to spend another action cancelling it. A 'what if' preview of a move would have shown the route, but a straight march order does not warn that it leaves my own country.

did: Ended turn 18 with my eight corps standing in Moravia/Vienna after beating Kutuzov and Charles (the turn before), the Russians' Bagration (46k) unscouted in the fog, and a second league war declared; I had used 'recruit' and 'attack' as usual.
expected: Some sign that my corps were spent (morale 9-14% after two days of forced battle) and that an unseen 46,000-man army was adjacent, or the chance to pull back before the end-turn.
saw: The enemy phase delivered seven battles in two turns: Bagration beat Ney, Massena, Bernadotte (captured), Lannes (captured), then Napoleon, Ney, Davout, Murat (army destroyed) and Massena (captured), one corps after another, Moravia and Ukraine lost, the Emperor down to 438 men. Nothing on the end-turn screen, the Dispatch or the top bar said my army was at 0-14% morale or that Bagration was near; the ledger showed it only after the damage. 'Our military dominance (+11)' was still quoted by Talleyrand afterwards. The corps system that won me every earlier battle also fed each beaten corps into the next fight.
